en: Udāna 7.3 Paṭhamasattasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

Now at that time, the people of Sāvatthī for the most part dwelt excessively attached to sensual pleasures—infatuated, greedy, fettered, infatuated, and clinging, having become completely absorbed in sensual pleasures.
Then, in the morning, a number of bhikkhus dressed, took their bowls and robes, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.

Having walked for alms in Sāvatthī, after their meal and returning from their almsround, they approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
Sitting there, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:

"Venerable sir, here in Sāvatthī, for the most part, people dwell excessively attached to sensual pleasures—infatuated, greedy, fettered, infatuated, and clinging, being completely absorbed in sensual pleasures."
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Beings attached to sensual pleasures, bound by the attachment to sensual pleasures,
do not see the fault in the fetters.”
"For those who are attached through the fetters and bonds will never cross over the vast and great flood. Thus [ends] the third [verse].
